{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Ethiopia|Cuisine of Ethiopia]]

'''Shiro wat''', sometimes called '''shiro wet''', is a traditional Ethiopian pea stew.

==Ingredients==
* ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Oil|oil]]
* 4 spoons [[Cookbook:Berbere|berberei]] (a spice mix with [[Cookbook:Chili Powder|red pepper powder]])
* 2½ cups [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* 4 spoons ''shiro'' powder (made from different cereals and beans, typically [[Cookbook:Pea|split green peas]])
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste
* 2 spoons [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] (optional)

==Procedure==
# Heat a medium-size [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|skillet]], add the onion, and cook for 1–2 minutes.
# Add the oil, and after 1 minute add berberei. Cook it for 4–5 minutes, stirring regularly and adding a dash of water if it tries to stick on the pan.
# Add the water.
# When the water [[Cookbook:Boiling|boils]], add the shiro, carefully stirring it in the pan; it should not make lumps. Then cook it for 5 minutes, stirring it regularly.
# Finally, add salt and the butter, and after 2–3 minutes, remove it from the heat.
# Served hot or cold with [[Cookbook:Injera|injera]].

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* Shiro powder can be bought from Ethiopian grocers.
* Alternatively, split green peas can be used—just extend the simmering period until the peas are tender and fall apart.
